column1: # B1183 (#502) -- the nine-step stand-byte table: the FABLE column (the ported
# StandState machine driven by its real feed points, measured by
# tests/test_stand_state.cpp TheLane5FullSequenceTable) beside the ORACLE
# column (the official client's +0x251 of the caster spawn, char 67, READ
# live on lane 5 by the /proc/pid/mem poller b1183_poll.py -- never inferred).
# Oracle evidence:
#   legA-fix5 (legs/legA-fix5/poll/poll.log): INIT byte +0x251 = 100;
#     (the Down release = stand). The measured crouch key is Down (VK_DOWN),
#     the client's live keymap -- fable's own duck key is C; the keys differ
#     between the two clients, the BYTES are what must match.
#   legA3_discovery: the byte NEVER left 100 through all of the letter-key
#     SIT/USE probes; the one write was WR 100->111 (SPACE = crouch). So no
#     probed LETTER key produces 110 (sit) or 105 (loot).
# FINDING 1 -- LETTER KEYS GO TO CHAT INPUT, NOT GAME ACTIONS (legA-fix5 is
# the controlled proof): in one leg, probe_down (Down arrow) produced WR
# 100->111 (duck) and, on release, 111->100, while probe_c / probe_x /
# probe_z (letter keys) produced NO byte write at all. The official client
# routes letter keys to the chat box; only arrow/special keys fire keydown
# actions. Consequence: the live-keymap bindings SIT_STAND k0='s' and USE
# k0='u' (below) are EFFECTIVELY DEAD as keydown triggers -- a 's'/'u' tap is
# typed into chat, not fired as an action (legE's opcode-confirmed 's'/'u'
# presses produced zero C->S movement/use packets). The official client's
# OWN sit/stand path is therefore the /sit and /stand CHAT COMMANDS (and the
# UI Sit/Walk buttons), which is what legF drove. (The card sanctions the
# /sit command; this states which method the client actually uses, measured.)
# FINDING 2 -- THE +0x251 BYTE IS A POSE BYTE; STUN DOES NOT CHANGE IT. The
# measured values are all poses: stand=100, sit=110, duck=111, loot=105.
# When the character is STUNNED, +0x251 HOLDS the current pose (100). legF
# proved the stun was genuinely applied server-side (S->C OP_Stun 0x1e51
# PLUS OP_PlayerStateAdd -- the stunned state flag -- PLUS a 60-byte
# OP_SpecialMesg), yet the byte held 100 through the whole 8 s window. So
# the official client tracks "stunned" as a separate state flag, NOT as a
# value in the stand/pose byte. FABLE writes 102 into the stand byte on the
# stun message (0x3050/0x3013), a value the official client's +0x251 never
# takes. This is the one measured FABLE-side difference (row below).
# FINDING 3 -- BENEATH-THE-WORLD LIMBO (environmental, since B1130). The
# zone now snaps the caster to z=3.875, BELOW the ground at -74,428 (the
# ground/heightmap data changed since B1127/B1130 ran fine at the same pose).
# In that "moving to safe point" state the character cannot enter
# stun/sit/loot states (legE: GM commands got opcode responses but the
# effects did not apply; the frame showed the character standing un-stunned).
# The POSE z is ignored by the snap; the escape is a SERVER-SIDE
# `#goto -74 428 10` (sets z=10 directly, above the ground), which legF used
# to get the caster into a valid, controllable state (sit/stand then worked).
# KEY DISCOVERY (legC3b, the corrected 267-slot live keymap dump) -- kept for
# the record; the decode is anchored three ways (DUCK 0xD0="DOWN"=INI
# KEYMAPPING_DUCK_1=208=the measured duck 111): SIT_STAND (action 138) k0
# high byte 0x1F='s'; USE (action 16) k0 high byte 0x16='u'; DUCK (action 12)
# k0 0xD0="DOWN". Per FINDING 1 the two letter bindings are dead keydown
# triggers; DUCK (Down) is the live one. The oracle INI sets BACK_2='s', so
# 's' is bound to both BACK and SIT_STAND (moot, since 's' is chat).
